1361: A few old squaws led meagre looking packhorses, and a dozen dirty, copper coloured youngsters, naked except for their breechcloths, hung to the horses' tails, to the straps that held the packs, or rode the travois — poles which were fastened to the sides of the horses and left to drag like the loose shafts of a buggy.
